Offline embedding refresh jobs are scheduled batch processes that regenerate vector embeddings for a corpus when the underlying embedding model changes or source documents update in bulk. They are a key operational pattern in vector-based retrieval systems.

## Core Characteristics

**Execution Model**
- Run on a fixed cadence (scheduled batch), not on-demand
- Re-embed the full document set or an incremental subset
- Operate outside the critical path of live queries

**Atomic Index Transition**
- New vectors are swapped into the retrieval index atomically
- Prevents serving mixed-model results mid-transition
- Ensures consistency across queries

## Operational Concerns

**Model Versioning**
- The embedding model version must be tracked and versioned per batch
- Enables tracking which model was used to generate each set of embeddings
- Critical for debugging and understanding quality changes

**Vector Drift Monitoring**
- Detect and measure drift between old and new vector representations
- Monitor degradation or improvement in retrieval quality
- Inform decisions about rollback or gradual rollout

**Safe Deployment**
- Staging the index swap behind a blue/green pattern enables rollback
- Quality regressions can be detected and rolled back before full deployment
- Provides an escape hatch if the new embeddings degrade retrieval performance

## Related Concepts

- [[Embedding-Versioning]] — managing model versions across batches
- [[Vector-Drift-Detection]] — monitoring changes in vector representations
- [[Blue-Green-Deployment]] — staged switching pattern used for index swaps
